source.title: Transformers Don't In-Context Learn Least Squares Regression
source.authors: Joshua Hill; Benjamin Eyre; Elliot Creager

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: Conceptually tests whether training-data and evaluation-distribution properties affect in-context learning, using regression-error and task-accuracy evaluations. It does not identify or manipulate induction heads or reproduce the original induction-head measurements.
record.gate_note: The paper reports regression performance under input-, weight-, scale-, and label-noise distribution changes, plus Caesar-cipher accuracy for frequent versus rare shifts. These bear on V5. The residual-stream spectral analyses characterize representations and their association with loss, but do not test induction-head claims; the signature–loss correlation is recorded as a finding for no version. Results cited from other work are not included.
record.test_reason: The study cites Olsson et al. and Elhage et al. only as background. It never identifies, ablates or tracks induction heads or previous-token heads. It does not measure loss against token index, phase changes or formation timing. Its results concern out-of-distribution generalization of linear-regression ICL (MSE under subspace, scale and label-noise shifts) and a residual-stream spectral signature. V5 asks whether and when induction heads form, and whether ICL persists. Here ICL forms in-distribution in every condition; only its OOD transfer is measured, which is a related but different construct. So no row measures what any version names, and the findings go under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors conclude that regression ICL hinges on coupling between pretraining data and residual-stream geometry, not on emulating OLS or GD. Structured subspace shifts cause large degradations. A spectral signature (two stable top singular directions) flags OOD prompts and correlates with low loss.
record.recipe_differences: Uses synthetic linear-regression training with distribution-shift evaluations and residual-stream spectral analysis, rather than induction-head identification, circuit analysis, or induction-head ablation.
record.method_sensitivity: Performance changes with input and weight subspace shifts, input magnitude, training-scale diversity, and label-noise setup; the real-task evaluation also differs by cipher-shift frequency.

fits_no_version.finding: Regression-ICL transformers degrade heavily under input-subspace, weight-subspace and input-scale shifts away from pretraining data. Multi-scale training reduces scale-shift degradation. Even in-distribution, overdetermined error is orders of magnitude above OLS.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Transformers trained for in-context linear regression generalize only within the span and scale of their pretraining distribution, unlike OLS or GD.

fits_no_version.finding: Qwen3-4B decodes shift-13 Caesar ciphers at 43% but shift-4 at 10% (150 prompts each).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: LLM in-context task performance drops for task variants presumed rare in pretraining.

fits_no_version.finding: A top-two singular-vector alignment score correlates with prompt loss (r=-0.557) and separates ID from OOD prompts (94.45% vs 19.39% inside the 95% region for T∥).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A residual-stream spectral signature predicts ICL regression failure under distribution shift.

record.peer_reviewed: ICML 2025 Workshop on Reliable and Responsible Foundation Models; accepted for oral presentation
record.problems: Evidence primarily concerns synthetic linear-regression prompts and GPT-2-style architectures; the authors state that generalization to richer real-world ICL tasks remains open. Several key error results are presented in figures without numerical values in the text. The Caesar-cipher extension uses 150 prompts per shift and reports no uncertainty. No induction-head measurement is performed.
record.rows_left_out: Spectral spectra, singular-vector alignment, Gaussian-region percentages, and readout projections are not separately rowed because they measure representation geometry rather than induction-head behaviour or ICL performance itself; the signature–loss correlation is included as r22. No other reported ICL-performance result was intentionally omitted.

untested.parts: No induction or previous-token heads identified; no copying mechanism tested.
No training dynamics, loss bump or phase change measured.
No attribution of ICL to induction heads.
No search for induction heads across models.
No measurement of whether or when induction heads form, or of ICL persistence over training. ICL exists in all conditions; only its OOD transfer is measured.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's V5 link conflates OOD generalization of ICL with V5's formation and persistence dependence; the paper has no induction-head content. Rows r9–r16 come from one figure with no numbers and an unidentified training scale. The paper is an ICML 2025 workshop paper.

versions.untested_parts: No induction heads are identified, tested, or shown to compose with previous-token heads or implement the copying pattern.
No induction-head formation dynamics, training-loss bump, or token-index in-context-learning transition is measured.
The study does not measure induction heads or test whether they account for most in-context learning in large transformers.
The paper does not test whether induction heads occur across model families, sizes, training runs, architectures, or modalities.

Tests whether regression ICL performance changes with training/evaluation distribution and setup, and reports a real-task frequency comparison. Does not test whether induction heads form, or when they form.
No few-shot task-learning mechanism is attributed to other heads or compared with induction heads.
No induction-head formation stages or overlapping transitions are measured.

relation.reason: Section 2 cites Olsson et al. and Elhage et al. as background; the experiments do not identify, ablate, or track induction heads.

tranche.reason: The study tests regression generalization and residual-stream spectral signatures, without testing or using induction heads. Its training-distribution results do not establish induction-head formation or persistence of induction-mediated ICL.

source_check.notes: The authors-conclusion paraphrase is accurate. Appendix I treats shift 13 as frequent and shift 4 as rare without measuring their pretraining frequencies; its accuracies do not measure induction-head behavior.
